subject: Physics
learning_outcomes: Differentiate between physical observables and derived mathematical representations
Apply New Cartesian Sign Convention systematically without relying on spatial intuition
Distinguish between charge conservation and energy dissipation in electrical networks
Identify geometric ray behavior at boundaries vs holistic object image formation
Differentiate magnetic field vectors, force vectors, and current directions using formal orthogonal vector rules

topics.name: Reflection of Light & Spherical Mirrors
core_formulas: f = R / 2 (Focal length and radius of curvature)

sign_conventions.u: Always negative for real objects situated in front of mirror
sign_conventions.real_inverted_image: v is negative, m is negative, h_prime is negative
sign_conventions.virtual_erect_image: v is positive, m is positive, h_prime is positive

topics.name: Refraction of Light & Spherical Lenses
core_formulas: n_21 = v_1 / v_2 = sin(i) / sin(r) (Snell's Law)

sign_conventions.real_inverted_image: v is positive (formed on opposite side), m is negative
sign_conventions.virtual_erect_image: v is negative (formed on same side as object), m is positive

chapters.chapter_title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

topics.name: Human Eye Anatomy and Vision Defects
core_concepts: Power of accommodation: Ciliary muscles alter focal length of crystalline lens
Near point = 25 cm; Far point = infinity (normal eye)
Myopia (short-sightedness): Image forms in front of retina; corrected by concave lens
Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): Image forms behind retina; corrected by convex lens
Presbyopia: Loss of accommodation due to aging; corrected by bi-focal lenses

topics.name: Dispersion, Atmospheric Refraction, and Scattering
core_concepts: Prism dispersion: Different wavelengths travel with different speeds in glass; Violet deviates most, Red deviates least
Rainbow: Combined dispersion, internal reflection, and refraction in water droplets
Atmospheric refraction: Continuous refractive index gradient causing apparent star displacement, twinkling, advanced sunrise (2 min) and delayed sunset (2 min)
Rayleigh Scattering: Intensity proportional to 1 / lambda^4; blue scatters most in clear atmosphere; red scatters least and penetrates haze/fog

topics.name: Current, Potential Difference, and Ohm's Law
core_formulas: V = I * R (Ohm's Law at constant temperature)
R = rho * (L / A) (Dependence on length, area, resistivity rho)
core_concepts: Electric current is the continuous rate of net charge flow through a cross section
Electrons move from negative to positive; conventional current flows positive to negative
Resistivity is an intrinsic material property (ohm-metre), independent of dimensions

topics.name: Circuit Combinations, Joule Heating, and Power
core_formulas: Series: R_s = R1 + R2 + R3; Current I is constant across all resistors; V_total = V1 + V2 + V3
Parallel: 1/R_p = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3; Voltage V is constant across all branches; I_total = I1 + I2 + I3
H = I^2 * R * t (Joule's Law of Heating)
P = V * I = I^2 * R = V^2 / R (Unit: Watt, W)

topics.name: Magnetic Fields and Field Lines
core_concepts: Magnetic field is a vector quantity having both magnitude and direction
Field lines emerge from North pole and enter South pole outside; travel South to North inside (continuous closed loops)
Field lines never intersect: two lines intersecting would imply two distinct compass deflection directions at a single point, which is physically impossible
Right-Hand Thumb Rule: Thumb indicates current direction; curled fingers indicate magnetic field line circles

topics.name: Solenoid, Lorentz Force, and Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
core_concepts: Solenoid produces uniform parallel magnetic field lines inside, identical to a bar magnet
Magnetic force F acts on a moving charge or current-carrying wire perpendicular to both field and current
Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Forefinger = Field (B), Center finger = Current (I), Thumb = Force/Motion (F)
Force is zero when conductor is parallel to magnetic field; maximum when perpendicular
Domestic circuit safety: Live wire (220V, red/brown), Neutral (0V, black/blue), Earth wire (green) protecting metal appliances from leakage current
